CompileOutcomeV2.description: The same engine-owned machine document, generation 2: a provider call happened in this round and `provenance.authoring` is its receipt. A fresh round that needed no call (an exact skeleton, a structured constant, the support grammar) and every replay answer generation 1 (CompileOutcome). No field grants authority, writes or executes source.

provenance.description: Reproduction metadata; neither program identity nor run evidence

authoring.description: Receipt of this round's provider calls; never workflow authority or run evidence

backend.description: Direct API receipt: provider and requested/observed model identities, request authority and usage completeness. Provider usage never proves an invoice. Additive fields may be absent on older servers.

cost_basis.description: No price or invoice is established by this authoring door: unpriced; billing_unverified. Token totals and their completeness are separate observations.

unreported_models.description: Responses that did not identify their model; never assumed to be the requested model or another invocation's observed model.

max_calls.description: The request bound this round ran under; null when none was configured (`source` says so): its requests were then counted without a count ceiling.

host.description: Configured endpoint host and optional port only; no user info, path, query or fragment. This does not authenticate a remote peer.

base_url_overridden.description: Effective configured URL differs from the provider profile seed; null if no seed comparison is available.

endpoint_basis.description: These endpoint fields describe operator configuration, independently from observed model identities.

calls.description: LOGICAL calls of the round. Each provider retry or structured-output fallback also consumes the physical-request grant recorded in backend.authority.http_requests; one invocation can send more than one authorized request.

context.description: What each logical call received, in call order: its role, the sha256 of its instruction and answer schema, its message bytes

input_tokens.description: Sum of reported counters from calls with complete base usage; null when no call reported both counters. If backend.usage_complete is false this is a partial observed sum, not the whole round.

model.description: The operator-seated authoring model (`provider/name`), never a caller's choice

output_tokens.description: Sum of reported counters from calls with complete base usage; null when no call reported both counters. If backend.usage_complete is false this is a partial observed sum, not the whole round.

decision.description: Bounded decision records: the native round's references, rounds and knowledge identity (hashes and selection, no host path)

plan.description: The record the round produced. A caller never sends it back: the server keeps it behind Nika-Compile-Replay

strategy.description: The internal strategy that settled the request (`native` for a seat-written candidate)

suggested_file.description: A file name for the candidate, never a path the compiler touched

cognition.description: The only cognition generation 1 accepts: no authoring model is contacted. On this server the explicit provider opt-in is generation 2 (CompileRequestV2)

CompileRequestV2.description: Generation 2 of the compile request, served only by a server whose operator seated native authoring (health `compileNativeV2`). Every generation-1 law holds: the encoded body follows the listener's configured HTTP body ceiling, without a smaller field-size or answer-count quota; unknown fields, a present null, duplicate keys and positional arrays are refused. New to this generation: a literal (an `answers` value, `change.set_constant.value`) that repeats an object key at any depth, or nests 128 or more arrays/objects deep (the JSON parser's recursion ceiling), is refused. No field names a model, endpoint, credential, host path, snapshot, strategy or plan: those are the operator's, and the plan a round produced stays on the server behind its replay token. Numbers are JSON integer literals (a fraction or an exponent is refused).

change.description: Edit only, exactly one of: `text`, a revision in any wording (not only a `Set const.NAME` sentence) that the round reads beside `original_intent`; or `set_constant`, one structured constant the core applies without a provider call

cognition.description: explicitProvider: one fresh round under the operator's seat or, with the `replay_token` of a round this server kept, that round's judged answer round: its plan is replayed with these `answers` and the seat is asked only to judge the replayed bytes, never to author again (an `intent.clarification` answer is refused; a candidate the seat does not accept forgets the token) · deterministicOnly: a zero-call replay of a round this server kept (requires `replay_token`, refuses `limits`): it repeats the round's exact input, its `answers` may answer the round's questions, and it never carries `intent.clarification` (409 compile_replay_input_changed)

limits.description: Optional limits for this explicitProvider round. They may only narrow the selected route capacities or an explicitly configured operator limit; above → 422 compile_limit, never clamped. No implicit request count, repair count or whole-round deadline is imposed.

call_timeout_ms.description: The wait for one model invocation; the transport does not resend automatically

deadline_ms.description: Explicit positive whole-round duration, absolute from admission and representable by the monotonic clock. Absent both caller and operator values, no whole-round deadline is imposed.

max_tokens.description: Positive output-token limit per completion, at most the selected route or explicit operator limit.

repairs.description: Explicit repair-round limit, narrowed from an operator limit when configured; zero disables repairs. Actual calls remain subject to max_calls when present.

max_calls.description: Explicit limit on physical HTTP requests and model invocations for this round, no more than any configured operator limit. Absent both values, requests are counted without a count ceiling.

mode.description: create requires `intent` and forbids `source`, `change` and `original_intent`; edit requires `source` and `change` and forbids `intent` and `workflow_id`

observed_world.description: Optional (health `compileObservedWorld`): what the caller's own engine observed of the files the request states, exactly the document `nika compile --observe-only <intent>` prints under `observed_world` (headers, key sets, short categorical values and kind counts, never a row). It rides the round as the CLI observer's own does: the seat authors against it, the grounding law grounds a rule's keys in it and the verifier reads it. Admitted only in that shape: every row about a path the request states (a source, a destination, or a tabular/JSON file directly inside a stated folder; a revision: its `original_intent` and change), keys and kinds the observer writes, a categorical value of at most 32 characters and 8 per column, at most 64 rows and 256 KiB serialized; anything else is refused whole (422 compile_observation_refused), never trimmed. It is part of the round's input: a replay or judged answer round repeats it byte for byte (another observation is another input, 409 compile_replay_input_changed). Refused beside `change.set_constant`.

original_intent.description: The request the base answered: required with `change.text` (the round reads the change beside the whole meaning), refused with `change.set_constant`

replay_token.description: The Nika-Compile-Replay header a fresh round of THIS server run answered. With deterministicOnly, a zero-call replay that asks no judge; with explicitProvider, the replay judged by the operator's seat (no authoring call), after which a candidate the seat did not accept forgets the token. Not an execution grant

trial_inputs.description: Optional, only beside `observed_world`, only on a server that lists `compileTrialInputs` (else 422 compile_trial_inputs_refused): the `trial_inputs` member of the same `nika compile --observe-only` document — the text of the files that observation marks `observed`, at most 1 MiB in all. The server writes them into a fresh scratch project of its own (removed when the round ends) and tries each final candidate there in the observed room `nika compile` and the Session use (no provider, network, process or gate; the originals are the caller's and untouched); the trial's report reaches the judge and the repairs, and a failed or missing trial is never `ready`. The bytes are never sent to a model and never echoed; the report the judge reads is the trial's own (`provenance.decision.rehearsal`). Part of the round's input like `observed_world`. A path no `observed` row names, a repeated path, an extra key or more than the bound is refused whole (422 compile_trial_inputs_refused).

info.description: Authenticated loopback remote execution, declarative schedules and stateless source-only authoring (POST /v1/compile never runs, admits or writes). This server's operator seated native authoring: POST /v1/compile also speaks compile_version 2 (health capability `compileNativeV2`), admits the caller's observation of the files its request states (`compileObservedWorld`) and, when the operator also seated a decision model, has it judge every candidate (`compileDecisionSeat`). Artifacts, schedule list/delete/trigger/backfill, /v1/arm, and POST /v1/run are absent.

post.description: The HTTP transport of the same Compile core as `nika compile`. Generation 1 (CompileRequest) is the foundation door, exactly as on a default server: deterministic, no provider contacted. Generation 2 (CompileRequestV2) exists only because this server's operator seated ONE native authoring model when building it (advertised by the `compileNativeV2` health capability). The operator may seat a decision model beside it (`nika serve --decision-model`, health `compileDecisionSeat`, the model never named): it then judges every candidate and answers the finite choices in place of the author, its requests on its own client outside the authoring grant; the receipt names it (`backend.decision_model`) and each verification attempt records the decision seat as its judge. A request may carry `observed_world`, the caller's own `nika compile --observe-only` document (health `compileObservedWorld`). A server that tries candidates (health `compileTrialInputs`) also admits `trial_inputs` beside it and tries each final candidate on them before it can be `ready`. `cognition: explicitProvider` opts in to one fresh round under that seat: the operator chose the model, its credential, its endpoint, the knowledge snapshot and the ceilings; a request names none of them and may only narrow the ceilings through `limits` (above an operator ceiling → 422 compile_limit, never clamped). A round has no implicit request count, repair count or whole-round deadline. Completion capacity follows the effective provider route. Operator or caller limits are honored; a caller may only narrow an explicitly configured operator ceiling. Invocations and physical requests are counted separately in backend.authority, including refusals; no redirect is followed, and provider retries or structured-output fallbacks consume the same physical-request grant. Repairs describe desired work, never permission to send more requests. Requested and provider-reported model identities are recorded separately; token usage is not an invoice. An explicitly configured deadline is absolute from admission: a round that must already stop never begins, and nothing it produces after it is answered or kept. A fresh round that leaves a native plan answers the header Nika-Compile-Replay: the whole input and plan are kept with no implicit count, size or expiry limit. An operator may explicitly limit the kept-round count and lifetime. `cognition: deterministicOnly` with that token and the round's exact input replays it with zero calls while retained by this server run. `cognition: explicitProvider` with that token, the round's exact input and its answers is the judged answer round: the kept plan is replayed with the answers and the seat only judges the replayed bytes (its judge calls, compile_version 2, never an authoring call); a candidate the seat does not accept is held and its token forgotten, so those bytes are never put to the same judge again through it. An explicit lifetime is never renewed by use; all tokens are forgotten on restart. A lost first answer leaves no token and a new fresh round spends again: there is no idempotency key and nothing retries. Version negotiation: a server without the capability answers compile_version 2 with 422 compile_version_unsupported; the answer's compile_version is 2 exactly when a provider call happened. Creates no job, run, approval, trace, file or permission. `check_preview` is a REVIEW of the source only: POST /v1/jobs judges a candidate again, by Check alone, never against the request: a candidate is proposed only when `status` is `ready`, and an `incomplete` one is a preview (CompileOutcome `candidate` and `diagnostics` name the verifier's `verify_held` and `verify_resume` markers). A document carrying the seat's own credential is refused whole (500 compile_disclosure_refused).

200.description: Authoring outcome — ready, incomplete and refused are all data. compile_version 2 (CompileOutcomeV2) exactly when a provider call happened; every other answer, replays included, is generation 1 (CompileOutcome)

Cache-Control.description: no-store on every answer to a generation-2 request, fresh round or replay, whatever its compile_version

Nika-Compile-Replay.description: Only on a fresh generation-2 round that left a native plan this server run keeps: the opaque token of that round (256 random bits, 64 lowercase hex). The whole input and plan have no implicit count, size or expiry limit; the operator may explicitly limit kept-round count and lifetime. Present it with cognition deterministicOnly and the round's exact input. An explicit lifetime uses the monotonic clock and is never renewed; every token is forgotten on restart and is never reflected in a refusal. Tokens require operating-system randomness. Not an execution grant and not a deduplication of paid work

408.description: request_timeout — the request deadline (body intake, generation 1, replays) · compile_deadline_exceeded — a fresh round's absolute deadline passed: its work stopped or never began, nothing was kept, and a provider call in flight may still be billed

409.description: compile_replay_unavailable — this server run keeps no round under that token (unknown, past an explicit lifetime, another run) · compile_replay_input_changed — a replay repeats its round's exact input and never replaces the intent · compile_context_changed — the pinned knowledge snapshot no longer reads as pinned; nothing was sent

422.description: malformed_compile_request · compile_version_unsupported · compile_mode_unsupported · compile_cognition_unsupported · compile_limit · compile_new_intent_required — an intent.clarification on a fresh generation-2 round: send the replacement as a new intent · compile_observation_refused — `observed_world` is not the observer's document of what the request states, or exceeds its bound: nothing was sent · compile_trial_inputs_refused — `trial_inputs` are not the text of the files `observed_world` marks observed, exceed 1 MiB, or this server tries no candidate: nothing was sent

500.description: internal_error — compiler machinery failure, nothing is echoed · compile_disclosure_refused — the outcome would carry a withheld credential and is refused whole

503.description: compile_busy — every compile slot is in use · compile_replay_capacity — the operator's explicit kept-round capacity is full; nothing was authored or spent · stopping — the server is stopping; the round stopped and nothing was kept
